jobs.excerpt: AXON Networks delivers a robust AI-driven, analytics-based orchestration platform and a wide portfolio of next-gen high-speed routers that leverage the newest Wi-Fi technologies.
jobs.description:
AXON Networks delivers a robust AI-driven, analytics-based orchestration platform and a wide portfolio of next-gen high-speed routers that leverage the newest Wi-Fi technologies. Together, these technologies give ISPs the ability to manage and troubleshoot their networks in real time, and to deliver an outstanding customer experience.

AXON Networks is a trusted strategic partner for its customers, helping them evaluate their current technologies and business models, and creating and executing strategies that enable them to innovate faster, accelerate their digital transformations, and strengthen their relationships with consumers.

AXON Networks is headquartered in Irvine, CA USA with Asia HQ in Singapore and also operating in Denmark, Spain and Vietnam.

The Network Operations Security Engineer serves as the designated Security Champion for Network Operations. The role translates enterprise security requirements, vulnerabilities, and threat information into actionable operational controls and coordinated remediation across production networks, cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes-based services, and device-management environments. The engineer partners with centralized Information Security, Engineering, DevOps, NOC, and Support to reduce operational security risk without compromising service reliability or customer availability.

This is an embedded, production-focused security engineering role—not ownership of the enterprise information security program, not a general compliance analyst position, and not a replacement for Engineering or system-owner responsibility to implement technical fixes.

Responsibilities

Security Champion and Information Security Partnership

  • Act as the designated Network Operations representative in the Security Champions Council; communicate security requirements, emerging threats, standards, and priorities to operational teams.
  • Coordinate with centralized InfoSec on risk classification, remediation deadlines, escalations, exceptions, evidence, and technical guidance.
  • Promote security awareness, practical controls, and repeatable secure operating practices within NOC, Support, and Operational Excellence.

Production Vulnerability Remediation

  • Assess how reported CVEs, scanner findings, misconfigurations, and exposures affect production network and infrastructure services; work with asset and service owners to confirm applicability and customer impact.
  • Coordinate remediation plans with Engineering, DevOps, Cloud Operations, and system owners; identify maintenance windows, dependencies, service risks, rollback requirements, and validation steps.
  • Track operational execution and provide verified closure evidence to InfoSec; escalate overdue or high-risk remediation while avoiding a duplicate enterprise vulnerability tracking program.

Operational Security and Change Readiness

  • Review production-impacting designs, releases, and changes for operational security readiness, including access, network exposure, segmentation, logging, monitoring, recovery, and rollback.
  • Identify negative/failure scenarios and security-sensitive operational dependencies; recommend controls and document residual risks for the appropriate approval authority.
  • Partner with Change Management and Operational Readiness functions to ensure secure deployment and post-change validation.

Network, Cloud and Infrastructure Security

  • Assess operational security posture of network devices, connectivity, management interfaces, cloud workloads, containers, Kubernetes, IAM, secrets, and service-to-service access within the supported environment.
  • Work with platform and network engineering owners to improve configuration baselines, privileged access, patching, network segmentation, telemetry, and resilience.
  • Help identify and reduce risk in CPE/device-management workflows, remote management, firmware rollouts, and associated production services where applicable.

Security Incident Readiness and Response

  • Participate in security-related production incidents, supporting scoping, triage, containment, recovery, customer-impact analysis, and evidence preservation under the enterprise incident response framework.
  • Coordinate NOC/Support/Engineering response and operational communications with InfoSec; support post-incident reviews and ensure operational corrective actions are completed.
  • Improve security-relevant alerts, runbooks, escalation paths, and operational response exercises.

Automation, Metrics and Continuous Improvement

  • Partner with Operational Excellence and automation engineers to reduce manual security checks and improve security-related monitoring and response workflows.
  • Maintain operational metrics for remediation execution, overdue actions, security change readiness, control coverage, and recurring security incidents; feed authoritative data into InfoSec reporting.
  • Drive lessons learned into monitoring, documentation, change procedures, and production

Required qualifications

  • 5+ years in network/infrastructure security engineering, production operations, cloud infrastructure, SRE, or a closely related technical role.
  • Strong understanding of TCP/IP, routing, DNS, TLS, firewalls, segmentation, access controls, and troubleshooting in production environments.
  • Practical experience assessing vulnerabilities, CVEs, exposure, risk, remediation planning, and validation; familiarity with vulnerability and cloud security tools.
  • Experience with production incidents, change management, rollback planning, operational readiness, and cross-functional engineering coordination.
  • Working knowledge of cloud environments, containers/Kubernetes, monitoring/logging, and infrastructure security concepts.
  • Ability to communicate technical risk and operational tradeoffs clearly to Engineering, Operations, and Information Security.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Telecom/broadband/ISP, CPE, gateways, routers, ONTs, Wi-Fi, ACS, TR-069, TR-369/USP, or fleet/device-management environments.
  • GCP or OCI experience; Kubernetes workload security; IAM, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, or DevSecOps collaboration.
  • Familiarity with Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7, Wiz, Orca, Prisma Cloud, Trivy, SIEM, or comparable tools.
  • Automation/scripting experience (Python, Bash, APIs); relevant certifications such as Security+, CISSP, CCSP, or GIAC.

Success Measures

  • Timely remediation of Network Operations-owned security actions within InfoSec-defined targets.
  • Fewer repeat security-related production incidents and unresolved operational exposures.
  • Security requirements consistently incorporated into production change and operational readiness reviews.
  • Improved security telemetry, runbooks, escalation readiness, and remediation validation.
  • Effective participation in the Security Champions Council and clear cross-team accountability.

This position is fully remote within North America. Please note that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Annual salary range: $120,000 - $175,000 USD

jobs.description:
MPLC provides a legal way to show movies and TV in public or commercial spaces across the globe. Our business has been running for over 30 years, and we are the number one trusted partner to studios and producers for public performance licensing. We work with every major Hollywood studio and hundreds of independents, and we are a key player in the entertainment and intellectual property ecosystem.

We are on a truly exciting journey as a company. We're growing quickly, investing in our teams, and have bold plans for the future. To support that growth, we're looking for a Customer Success Executive to join our Customer Success Team.

The job in two bullet points:
  • Own a portfolio of existing customers and take direct accountability for minimizing churn within that book, alongside driving renewal and expansion revenue.
  • Ensure coverage completeness by confirming every customer site and location, including newly added ones, is properly covered by their license.

You will love this job if...

  • You have 2-5 years of experience in customer success, account management, or licensing, with a track record of managing renewals and mitigating churn.
  • You are comfortable handling commercial objections, including cost-driven pushback, in a calm and consultative way.
  • You have strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • You are comfortable working across internal teams and directly with client contacts at varying seniority levels.
  • You are proficient with CRM tools.
  • You are comfortable with a high volume of proactive outbound calls as a core, everyday part of the role.
  • Experience with licensing, media, or intellectual property is a plus.

Let's be honest!
This is a proactive, commercially focused customer success role. You will be responsible for renewal and expansion revenue, minimizing churn, confirming coverage accuracy, handling objections, and following up on payment. Collected revenue, not simply a signed renewal, is what counts toward your book of business and your results in this role.
As a function, this team is a net revenue retention play. The goal is to move net revenue retention from 102% to 105% in Year 1, calculated as expansion plus renewal minus churn. Individual measures roll up to the team's overall net revenue retention target, not a standalone quota.

If you need a bit more information...

This position runs on a structured outbound calling cadence, proactively checking in with every customer approximately 90 days ahead of their renewal date to confirm coverage, catch any new sites or locations, and resolve compliance questions well before renewal.

You will monitor customer usage declarations against public sources, provide compliance assurance, handle renewal objections, identify and close upsell opportunities, and take direct ownership of ensuring customer invoices are paid in full and on time. You will also coordinate with Legal and Finance on deal amendments and documentation, maintain accurate CRM records, and escalate the most complex renewal objections, compliance questions, or at-risk accounts to a senior colleague.

  • Remote located in the United States

Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk.

Principal Product Security Researcher

Imagine a world where we’re not just reacting to the latest security headline, but shaping the future threat landscape so our customers sleep better at night (and so do we).

As a Principal Product Security Researcher at Chainguard, you’ll lead our product security research function end-to-end: mapping emerging threats, turning insight into strategy, and helping Chainguard stay several moves ahead of attackers across our entire product portfolio.

The role, in a nutshell

Chainguard prioritizes our customers’ security above all else, which means preparing not just for the attacks of today, but for those of tomorrow as well. In this Principal-level role, you’ll:

  • Own the product security research agenda for Chainguard scanning the broader ecosystem, identifying emerging attack patterns, and translating them into clear risks and opportunities for Chainguard and our customers.
  • Shape security direction across products and platforms, partnering closely with Product, Engineering, and Security leadership to embed your findings into roadmaps, architecture decisions, and long-term plans.
  • Drive the agenda and discussion topics across the whole industry, helping everyone to understand what is important, where the risks are, and why they should pay attention.

If you enjoy turning ambiguous, fast-moving threat intel into concrete, multi-quarter plans that change how a company operates, this is your playground.

  • Research emerging threats & trends in software supply chain and product security, and analyze their impact on Chainguard’s products and customers.

jobs.description:
Description

TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We’ve been doing it for over five years, teaching complete beginners — people with no prior tech background — through cohort-based programs built on our own platform and curriculum, developed in partnership with Nebius AI. Our team is fully remote and globally distributed, and we serve a large, active student base across both regions.

As a Technical Owner you’ll own every technical decision behind our programs, from the first conversation with a course author to the bug that never reaches a learner. This is a technical partner role, not a coding job: you weigh each decision against cost, time to learner, and bugs shipped, and you lead one engineer who writes autotests. The role is fully remote and full-time, for candidates based outside the US.

What you will do

  • Own each program’s technical setup. Know its environments, services, providers, and autotests, and keep a written map of what each program depends on.
  • Shape new and updated programs. Collect requirements from authors and constraints from product, test the options, and land on a workable trade-off.
  • Replace what no longer fits. Find, cost, and run the switch when a tool, provider, or setup is outdated or too expensive.
  • Manage providers. Compare offers, negotiate terms, and own integrations with external providers.
  • Lead autotest coverage. Set coverage and priorities for the autotest engineer, and write or fix tests yourself when needed.
  • Be our customer to engineering. Write specs with acceptance criteria for automation, API, and platform needs, and chase each one to done.
  • Cut bugs reaching learners. Trace each bug to where it entered, close the gap with a test, check, or process change, and track the trend.

Requirements

Must have

  • End-to-end technical ownership. 3+ years in engineering, QA automation, or technical operations, including choosing a product’s setup and living with the trade-off after launch.
  • Solid mid-level coding. Python and TypeScript/JavaScript, Git, CI, containers, and REST APIs: enough to read unfamiliar code, fix bugs, and write autotests.
  • English for requirements work. Strong enough to run requirements sessions and write specs engineering teams accept without a round of questions.

Nice to have

  • Leading engineers. Leading or mentoring at least one engineer, ideally in test automation.
  • EdTech and content validation. LMS or autograded courses, QA or release work, or agents that check content for accuracy and freshness.
  • Automation and data stack. Claude Code, MCP, n8n or Make; SQL and dashboards.

What we can offer you

  • Ownership. Real decision-making power in your area: we trust your expertise and don’t micromanage.
  • Remote and flexible. Fully remote collaboration
  • Digital office. Slack, Notion, Miro, and Zoom, with every license you need.

jobs.description:
Mirantis, an IREN company, is the Kubernetes-native AI infrastructure company, enabling organizations to build and operate scalable, secure, and sovereign infrastructure for modern AI, machine learning, and data-intensive applications. By combining open-source innovation with deep expertise in Kubernetes orchestration, Mirantis empowers platform engineering teams to deliver composable, production-ready developer platforms across any environment — on-premises, in the cloud, at the edge, or in sovereign data centers.

As enterprises navigate the growing complexity of AI-driven workloads, Mirantis delivers the automation, GPU orchestration, and policy-driven control needed to manage infrastructure with confidence and agility. Committed to open standards and freedom from lock-in, Mirantis ensures that customers retain full control of their infrastructure strategy.

Job Description

We are looking for an experienced DevOps Engineer to own the deployment, release, and reliability backbone of the k0rdent-ai platform — our multi-tenant control plane for enterprise GPU infrastructure. The platform’s core services — identity (Keycloak), API gateway (Kong), workflow engine (Temporal), a suite of Go APIs, and the PostgreSQL databases behind them — run on every control-plane and regional cluster we operate, and must be upgraded safely, observed continuously, and recovered quickly.

You will run this platform across both cloud Kubernetes (AWS) and bare-metal clusters in our data centers, delivering it through Helm charts and k0rdent ServiceTemplates and MultiClusterServices. Beyond day-to-day operations, a substantial focus of this role is engineering the foundations that stateful services depend on: snapshot-capable storage (CSI drivers, StorageClasses, volume snapshots), CloudNativePG backups and point-in-time recovery, and the CI/CD and bare-metal end-to-end pipelines that validate every change before it reaches customers.

Because this platform holds the record of every tenant, user, and cluster action, this role also owns its operational readiness — runbooks, restore drills, and the upgrade and rollback paths that keep a failed release from turning into data loss.

Main Responsibilities

  • Multi-Environment Kubernetes Operations: Deploy, upgrade, and operate k0s / k0rdent-managed Kubernetes clusters on AWS and on bare-metal hardware, across a global control plane and multiple regions — cluster lifecycle, node maintenance, capacity planning, and version upgrades.

  • Helm & Service Delivery: Author and maintain Helm charts and k0rdent ServiceTemplates and MultiClusterServices for core services (Keycloak, Kong, Temporal, CloudNativePG, and in-house Go APIs), including dependency ordering, health gating, versioning, and zero-downtime upgrade paths.

  • Storage & Snapshot Engineering: Design and run Kubernetes storage for each environment — AWS EBS CSI in the cloud; OpenEBS LocalPV, Longhorn, or Ceph on bare metal — including StorageClasses, reclaim policies, the CSI snapshot controller, and VolumeSnapshotClasses, so stateful services can be snapshotted and restored reliably.

  • Database Backup & Recovery: Operate CloudNativePG backup and recovery end to end — scheduled volume snapshots, continuous WAL archiving to object storage, point-in-time recovery, and replica clusters — with defined RPO/RTO targets and regular restore drills.

  • CI/CD & End-to-End Testing: Build and maintain GitHub Actions pipelines for linting, chart unit tests, artifact packaging and publishing to OCI registries, and on-demand bare-metal end-to-end environments; keep them fast, reliable, and easy to debug.

  • GitOps & Infrastructure as Code: Maintain a strictly declarative infrastructure-as-code (IaC) culture using Terraform and Argo CD (or Flux), keeping every environment — from developer labs to production — reproducible and reviewable through code.

  • Observability & Incident Response: Build monitoring and alerting (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry) for service health, database replication and backup status, and capacity; join the on-call rotation, lead troubleshooting, and drive post-incident improvements.

  • Security & Air-Gapped Delivery: Manage TLS and certificate lifecycle (cert-manager), secrets, network policies, and least-privilege RBAC, and support private-registry and air-gapped installations for sovereign customers.

Qualifications

Must Have

  • Platform Experience: 8+ years in DevOps, SRE, or platform engineering, including 3+ years operating production Kubernetes for business-critical services.

  • Kubernetes Depth: Strong grasp of Kubernetes primitives — workloads and StatefulSets, operators and CRDs, persistent volumes and CSI storage, RBAC, and network policies — with hands-on experience upgrading and troubleshooting clusters in production.

  • Helm & Release Engineering: Hands-on authoring of non-trivial Helm charts — templating, values design, chart dependencies, and testing with helm-unittest or chart-testing. Experience with k0rdent, Cluster API, or a multi-cluster delivery tool (Argo CD ApplicationSets, Fleet, Sveltos) is preferred, but what matters is depth with Helm, not the specific delivery tool.

  • Kubernetes Storage: Practical experience with CSI drivers, StorageClasses, and volume snapshots — AWS EBS CSI preferred, but equivalent experience with Longhorn, Ceph (Rook), OpenEBS, or another cloud CSI driver is acceptable. What matters is understanding how storage behaves when pods, nodes, and clusters fail.

  • PostgreSQL on Kubernetes: Hands-on experience running PostgreSQL through a Kubernetes operator — CloudNativePG (CNPG) preferred, but Zalando’s postgres-operator, Crunchy PGO, or a comparable operator is acceptable — including backups, restores, and point-in-time recovery.

  • Cloud Infrastructure: Production experience in AWS (EC2, EBS, VPC, IAM, S3; EKS a plus); equivalent GCP or Azure experience also counts.

  • CI/CD & Automation: Designing and maintaining GitHub Actions (or GitLab CI) pipelines, with solid scripting in Bash plus Python or Go (Golang).

  • Collaboration: Clear written and spoken English and comfort working across time zones, with regular overlap with US and European teams.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with bare-metal provisioning (Metal3, Ironic, PXE) and GPU or AI infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with Kong Gateway or the Kubernetes Gateway API, and Keycloak / OIDC identity integration.

  • Experience operating Temporal or other workflow engines in production.

  • Experience delivering software into air-gapped or sovereign environments using private registries and mirrored artifacts.

  • Experience designing cross-region disaster recovery for stateful services, including RPO/RTO trade-off decisions.

  • Certifications such as CKA / CKS or AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional — a plus.

  • Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects (Helm charts, Kubernetes operators, CNCF projects) — a huge plus.

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science & Engineering (or a related field), or 8+ years of equivalent related experience.

We offer:

  • Operate some of the most advanced AI infrastructure environments in production today.
  • Work with the latest NVIDIA GPU technologies, Kubernetes platforms, and high-performance networking environments.
  • Help define operational standards and reliability practices for next-generation AI infrastructure services.
  • Influence the adoption of AI-powered operational capabilities through k0rdent AI.
  • Work alongside highly skilled engineers solving complex infrastructure and platform challenges at scale.
  • Join a growing organisation investing heavily in AI infrastructure, platform services, and operational innovation.

Overview: Multi-Tenant Cloud Infrastructure Design

The Cloud Architect is responsible for designing, managing, and optimizing the entire multi-tenant cloud infrastructure that hosts our integrated supply chain e-commerce platform. While our current stack utilizes Oracle Cloud Free VMs, this role requires expertise in major public clouds (AWS/GCP/Azure) to architect scalable, resilient, cost-optimized, and compliant solutions that handle fluctuating e-commerce traffic, stable internal tool usage, and intensive AI agent compute demands.

Internship Details

Duration: 3 months

Start Date: Immediate

Location: Remote

Stipend: None initially. Based on your first-quarter performance, you may be offered a paid full-time opportunity, or even be absorbed directly by the client as an FTE.

Key Responsibilities & Core Projects

You will design and govern the platform's foundation, ensuring scalability and compliance across all environments.

  • Cloud Architecture Design: Design and evolve the target cloud infrastructure (utilizing AWS, GCP, or Azure best practices) for maximum scalability, security, and high-availability, ensuring the platform can reliably support the MES $\rightarrow$ WMS $\rightarrow$ OMS flow.

  • Capacity Planning & Optimization: Plan and optimize resource allocation to effectively handle unpredictable e-commerce traffic spikes and the specific compute requirements for AI agent training and inference, driving cost efficiency.

  • High Availability & Disaster Recovery (DR): Implement multi-region/multi-AZ high-availability architectures and define comprehensive Disaster Recovery (DR) strategies for all core services, including PostgreSQL 15 and Redis.

  • Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) Governance: Establish and enforce best practices for Terraform usage, ensuring configuration consistency, security compliance, and auditable infrastructure changes.

  • Security & Compliance: Conduct regular security reviews of cloud configurations (e.g., IAM, VPC/VNet, Storage) and ensure architecture aligns with data residency and compliance requirements relevant to our multi-tenant operations.

  • Service Integration: Architect the network and service mesh overlay that integrates the containerized applications (Docker/Traefik) with external cloud services and the overall monitoring solution (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry).

Required Technologies & Tools

Candidates must possess deep architectural experience with public cloud providers and infrastructure automation:

  • Cloud Providers: Expert-level proficiency in at least one major public cloud (AWS, GCP, or Azure).

  • Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC): Mandatory expertise in Terraform for cloud resource provisioning.

  • Containerization: Deep knowledge of Docker networking, security, and orchestration principles.

  • Networking & Edge: Experience configuring load balancing, service mesh, and ingress controllers (e.g., Traefik).

  • Data & Storage: Architecting scalable database services (PostgreSQL) and object storage (MinIO).

  • Security: Cloud security best practices, IAM policy design, and network segmentation.

AI Agent Focus

You will optimize the cloud layer for our emerging AI capabilities.

  • Compute Optimization: Design elastic and cost-effective compute clusters (e.g., GPU instances) to efficiently handle the variable demands of LLM fine-tuning and multi-agent system orchestration.

  • Data Residency: Architect the data pipeline and storage solutions to ensure that training data and model artifacts adhere to strict data residency requirements across tenants.

Success Metrics & Career Path

Performance will be measured by:

  • Cost Efficiency: Demonstrable reduction in cloud operational costs (FinOps) while maintaining performance.

  • Availability: Achieving defined SLAs/SLOs for infrastructure uptime and performance.

  • Compliance: Successful implementation and auditing of cloud security and data residency controls.

Mentorship Structure: Reports to the Solution Architect or Head of Technology, collaborating closely with the SRE and DevSecOps teams to operationalize cloud strategy.

About SuperchargeMe

SuperchargeMe is one brain for the whole commerce business. Ten products, Ads-IQ, Retention-IQ, Restock-IQ, Stores-IQ, Marketplaces-IQ, Crossborder-IQ, NPD-IQ, Concierge-IQ, Feeds-IQ and Partnership-IQ, share one set of numbers. They don't stop at recommendations: they make the changes too, at the level of control each brand chooses. It works inside Slack, plugs into 100+ tools from Shopify and NetSuite to Meta, Google and Amazon, and is running 23 brands today across paid media, retention, inventory and wholesale, stores, marketplaces, catalog and partnerships.

Every function has a tool. Nothing runs the whole. We built SuperchargeMe to run the whole.

The product is live and brands are paying for it. Selling it full-time is the next step. That's you.

The role in a sentence

You'll be the first person selling SuperchargeMe full-time: finding mid-market omnichannel brands that haven't heard of us, getting meetings with their leadership, and closing deals on numbers the CFO can sign off.

Where we are

SuperchargeMe is already revenue-generating, with brands paying for it every month. Case studies from our first clients are being written now. Until now the founders have sold it themselves. You'll take over the deals and conversations they've started, then build a much bigger pipeline with your own outbound, contacts and partner introductions.

Who you sell to: mid-market omnichannel brands, roughly $20M to $300M in revenue, primarily in the US with UK and EU brands too, selling across their own store, marketplaces, wholesale and retail. Brands starting with a single product sign up on their own. Brands that want several platforms working together, with onboarding, come to you.

There's no sales team or SDRs yet, and what works in a sale is still in the founders' heads. Writing it down is part of the job. A founding Growth Marketer joins at the same time to bring in demos. A Chief Revenue Officer will join as we grow, and you'll be the first seller on the team they build.

Most brand leaders recognize the problem as soon as you describe it: ten or twenty tools, several with their own AI, all reporting different numbers. We call it the Silo Tax. Putting a number on it for every brand you meet is the job.

The work

  • Take over the deals and conversations the founders have started, then build on them with your own target accounts, outbound, contacts and introductions from agencies, Shopify partners and systems integrators.
  • Run each deal from first call to signature: discovery, an ROI case built on the brand's own numbers, a live demo, a trial, negotiation and close.
  • Keep the risk low for buyers with short trials, a phased setup and a clear plan for what they'll see in the first 30 days.
  • Show finance and operations leaders what connecting Shopify, their ERP, ad platforms and marketplaces is worth in margin, inventory and cash.
  • Start each customer on whichever product proves value fastest, then add more. Brands that signed up on their own for one product are good candidates.
  • Write down what wins and loses deals, so the next sellers have a playbook and the product team hears what buyers want.

What good looks like

We'll judge you on new revenue you found and closed yourself.

  • In your first month you can demo the product without help, you've agreed a target list with the founders, and your first meetings with senior people are booked.
  • By the end of your first quarter your pipeline has grown well beyond what you took over, with trials running and your first deals closed.
  • Buyers who had never heard of us take your second meeting.
  • The founders stop joining your first calls, because they don't need to.

What you bring

  • Five or more years selling B2B software, with at least three as a mid-market or commercial Account Executive on 60 to 90 day sales cycles and contracts in the five to six figures.
  • Proof that you've beaten your number, such as commission statements or how you ranked against other sellers.
  • Deals won with buyers who had never heard of your company, with most of your closed revenue coming from leads you found yourself.
  • You're comfortable talking to finance and operations leaders about margin, inventory, cash and payback.
  • Your own relationships with senior people at mid-market omnichannel brands.
  • A working knowledge of the commerce stack: Shopify, NetSuite or another ERP, Meta, Google and Amazon ads, and email and SMS tools.
  • You use AI tools and agents in your own selling and can show us how. We sell AI agents, so we'd expect that.

Bonus points

  • You've been one of a startup's first three salespeople.
  • You've sold at companies like NetSuite, Celigo, Wunderkind, Feedonomics, Bloomreach, Daasity, Extensiv, Brightpearl, Skio or Okendo.

Skip this one if

  • You need inbound leads and a famous logo to open doors.
  • You want a finished playbook, an enablement team and SDRs from day one.
  • You'd rather demo features than build an ROI case a CFO signs off.
  • You'd rather manage a book than build one.

Why join

  • You'll set how we sell: the pitch, the playbook and the feedback that shapes pricing. Every seller after you will build on it.
  • Most brand leaders haven't yet seen AI that takes actions on their business. You'll be the one showing them.
  • You'll work directly with both founders, who ran commerce brands before building software. Deals get decided quickly, and what buyers tell you reaches the product fast.
  • Commission has no cap, contracts grow as customers add products, and you get stock options in the company you're helping build.

How we hire

  • A 30-minute intro call with the co-founders.
  • A deal deep-dive: talk us through two deals you found and closed yourself, with proof of what you hit.
  • A mock first call where you pitch a CFO who has never heard of SuperchargeMe.
  • References, including a former manager.

What you get

$110,000–$140,000 base · $220,000–$280,000 OTE

50/50 base and variable, uncapped commission, stock options so you own a real piece of what you build, and a strong benefits package.

Remote within the United States, with travel to client meetings and industry events, and some calls on UK and EU hours.

jobs.excerpt: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale.
jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

The Opportunity:

Grafana Labs is looking for a technically fluent engineer who loves building powerful demos, explaining complex systems clearly, and helping SRE and platform engineering leaders understand the value of our open approach to observability.

As Grafana’s offering shifts from dashboards to industry-leading agentic observability, our Product Marketing team is responsible for closing the gap between what our products can do and how customers understand that value. That means building clear, consistent positioning, enabling sellers with trustworthy technical narratives, and creating content that helps Platform Engineering teams quickly grasp why Grafana Cloud is the right choice for them.

As a Technical Product Marketer you will play a critical part in that transformation. You’ll be the hands-on engineer who brings our technical story to life for buyers, not just practitioners. You’ll build core demos, run technical workshops and webinars, and act as the technical bridge between our Product and Sales orgs. Your work will help SRE and platform engineering leaders evaluate Grafana with confidence, equip sales engineers with better tools and talk tracks, and ensure our technical value shows up clearly and consistently across the entire customer journey.

This is a unique chance to shape how Grafana tells its story as we evolve our positioning in the AI era, strengthen seller enablement, and build a repeatable system for communicating product value.

What You'll Be Doing:

Build strategic, buyer-focused demos, videos, workshops, and webinars

  • Create and maintain polished, narrative-driven demos that highlight Grafana’s value for SRE and platform engineering leaders.
  • Record high-quality technical demo videos and walkthroughs in partnership with our video and content teams.
  • Lead webinars, workshops, and technical sessions designed for evaluators.
  • Teach customers not just how Grafana works, but why our approach is differentiated and valuable.
  • Use AI tools to generate variations, summaries, and reusable assets that scale technical content across channels.

Enable Solutions (Sales) Engineers with clear, consistent technical storytelling

  • Serve as PMM’s technical liaison to the SE org, ensuring consistent messaging and demo guidance.
  • Produce technical enablement assets, value-driven talk tracks, competitive narratives, and demo best practices.
  • Help SEs and sellers communicate Grafana’s story with clarity, confidence, and differentiation.

Collaborate with PMMs to drive technical buyer engagement across high-impact channels

  • Partner with PMMs to identify the most important buyer personas, problems, and technical messages, and help shape the content strategy needed to reach them.
  • Extend technical narratives into impactful buyer-facing channels including analyst briefings (Gartner, Forrester), industry forums, podcasts, conferences, and online technical communities.
  • Bring a technical perspective to PMM planning—helping ensure our content, campaigns, and enablement reflect the real challenges and priorities of SREs and engineering leaders.

Use automation & AI to scale technical content

  • Partner with software engineers to streamline demo setup, content workflows, and asset updates through workflows, agents, scripts, and AI-driven tools.
  • Use automation to make technical content more repeatable, discoverable, and scalable across teams.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

  • 5+ years in a technical role (solutions engineering, SRE, DevOps, backend engineering, technical PMM, or similar).
  • Interest and ability to travel to training and customer events 10-12 weeks per year.
  • Strong understanding of observability concepts and the needs of SRE/platform teams.
  • Ability to translate deep technical concepts into clear, value-focused stories.
  • Experience presenting technical content through demos, workshops, or webinars.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with a crisp, structured, persuasive style.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration; comfort working with PMM, Product, SEs, DevRel, and Field Engineering.
  • High ownership mindset with the ability to drive projects from concept to completion.
  • Comfort with light scripting or workflow automation.

Bonus Points For:

  • Hands-on experience with Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Mimir, Tempo, or similar observability tools, or a background in Observability or Platform Engineering.
  • Prior experience in Sales Engineering, DevRel, or technical product marketing.
  • Familiarity with demo environment automation or infrastructure-as-code tools.
  • Exceptional live presentation or workshop facilitation skills.

Compensation & Rewards:

In the US, the base compensation range for this role is $183,858 - $220,630. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.

CancerNavigator is an early-stage healthcare company (remote, headquartered in Washington, D.C.) dedicated to supporting cancer patients in their hour of need.

Our Mission & Our Work, in Brief

Cancer is the number one cause of death for commercially insured Americans and the top cost driver for health plans. And, cancer patients are struggling.

CancerNavigator is a white-glove, end-to-end, cancer support service for patients and their families. We work with health plans across the country to provide 1-1 support to members facing a cancer diagnosis. All of our support is delivered through dedicated Oncology Certified Nurses, who work with members to catch cancer early, get them to fantastic experts for their care, and help them through the thousands of other problems patients and their families face.

Join us to help serve cancer patients in their hour of need.

The “Nurse Navigator” Role

Our oncology nurse navigators are the front-line of CancerNavigator’s patient service. Nurse Navigators support patients at all parts of their journey – newly diagnosed, in active treatment, and entering remission. With more specificity, oncology nurse navigators:

  • Educate cancer patients (and their families) about their diagnosis, treatment options, and provide helpful information on any related questions and concerns the patient may have
  • Work closely with the researchers on our team to deliver tailored information to patients, guiding them to the centers and doctors that would be a great option for the patient’s care
  • Do everything possible to address any barriers to care (e.g. registering and scheduling appointments, coordinating with their health plan or their care team, transferring records, etc.)
  • Provide longitudinal support to the patient throughout their journey – helping them solve any issues related to their cancer diagnosis and care – whether connecting patients to mental health support, finding resources to ease the financial burden, arranging transportation to appointments, or answering any questions that may arise

The Requirements

The main requirement of this role is oncology nursing experience and a passion for serving cancer patients. More specifically, we are looking for someone with the following experience and qualifications:

  • Ability to work Pacific hours (8am-5pm PST)
  • Native Spanish Speaker
  • 3+ years of oncology nursing experience
  • Mastery of common navigation and care coordination issues (registration, scheduling, clinical department navigation, insurance coordination, solving coverage issues, etc.)
  • Mastery of basic computer tools (Gmail, Zoom, Word, PowerPoint, etc.)
  • Preferred: Oncology Certified Nurse (OCN)

Compensation and Benefits

  • Starting Salary Range: $100-115k (based on skills and experience)
  • Dental and Healthcare (80% employer paid), Vision Insurance (100% employer paid)
  • Healthcare and Dependent Care FSA
  • Group Life and AD&D Insurance (involuntary with the option to buy up coverage)
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Remote-first work; live where you want within the continental US
  • All-company on-sites 2x per year (in Washington DC and Denver)

Our Culture & Values, In Brief

We’re building a company where what we do matters. The goal couldn’t be clearer – serve cancer patients. As the business grows, and the work becomes more complex, we need to become more, not less, committed to why we are doing this.

We have three company values, which guide our work:

  1. Patients first, always: In everything we do, we put the cancer patient (and their families) first; we exist to serve them in their most urgent moments.
  2. Respect for our responsibility: We strive, as a team, to respect the gravity of the responsibility we bear to patients, always acting and producing in a way that is worthy of the trust they have placed in us.
  3. Kindness to and respect for others: We treat our teammates well, no exceptions. We are one team.

At CancerNavigator, we believe a well-rounded and diverse team is a key to our success. We never discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, or marital, veteran, or disability status.

About the Job:

We're looking for a Revenue Operations Manager, EMEA to be the go-to operator for our EMEA GTM team. This is a high-impact, highly visible role for someone who wants to shape how a growing region runs, from the first marketing touch to the closed deal and beyond.

## Senior Product ManagerAustin, TX or Remote (US) | Full-time | Salary + Equity## About the RoleThis is one of the most important hires at Suppli. We're looking for a Senior Product Manager who wants the autonomy and impact of a founding product role, with direct ownership of one or two of our core products.You won't just manage a roadmap — you'll define the vision and strategy for your product area, establish what success looks like, and own execution from customer discovery through launch and iteration. You'll work closely with our Head of Product, founders, engineers, and commercial teams to solve meaningful problems for our customers.We're a fast-moving company with an ambitious engineering team. We need someone who can turn customer insights and business opportunities into clear product direction, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and give engineers the context they need to build exceptional software.We're looking for someone who thinks in outcomes, moves fast, and uses AI not as a buzzword but as a daily multiplier — to prototype, design, analyze, and build.---## Who Thrives Here* You think like an owner, not a feature manager. You're comfortable taking responsibility for an entire product area — from understanding customer problems and setting priorities to defining the roadmap and delivering measurable results. You don't need someone telling you what to build next.* You can move from idea to prototype quickly. When you have a product hypothesis, you find ways to validate it before committing significant engineering resources. Whether that's a clickable flow, an AI-assisted prototype, or a functional proof of concept, you make ideas tangible.* You're analytical and decisive. You break down ambiguous problems, evaluate tradeoffs, and make decisions grounded in customer insights, data, and business impact. You know when to investigate further and when to move.* You define success before you build anything. You don't write a PRD without first asking: What does good look like? How will we know if this worked? What's the leading indicator we'll track in week one versus month three? You use metrics to drive decisions, not simply report results.* You're AI-native, not AI-curious. You use AI tools regularly to accelerate your work — whether that's prototyping, exploring designs, analyzing feedback, drafting specifications, or building internal tools. You're resourceful and don't wait for perfect conditions to make progress.* You have a bias for action. You prioritize execution over perfection, move quickly from discovery to delivery, and take full ownership of both outcomes and setbacks.* You communicate with clarity at every level. Whether you're speaking with customers, engineers, Sales, or the founding team, you can articulate the problem, explain your reasoning, and align people around a clear direction.* You thrive in a high-ownership environment. We're building an ambitious company together. You take initiative, embrace responsibility, and step up when it matters.## What You'll Own* Own the vision and strategy for your product area. Take end-to-end responsibility for one or two of Suppli's core products. Understand the customer, define the product vision, build and prioritize the roadmap, and drive meaningful business outcomes. You'll have significant autonomy while partnering closely with our Head of Product on broader company priorities.* Define what success looks like. Establish clear success metrics, leading indicators, and measurable outcomes for your initiatives. Make sure Engineering and stakeholders understand why we're building something and how we'll know whether it worked.* Turn customer problems into product direction. Conduct user interviews, analyze customer feedback, and identify opportunities to solve high-impact problems. Translate qualitative and quantitative insights into clear priorities and actionable product decisions.* Drive execution from concept to launch. Own the entire product development lifecycle, from discovery and requirements through scoping, development, release, and iteration. Work closely with Engineering and Design to ship high-quality customer-facing software.* Prototype before you spec. Use AI-assisted tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Lovable to explore concepts, validate hypotheses, and communicate product ideas. You don't need to be an engineer, but you should be comfortable using modern tools to move faster.* Build a culture of measurement and experimentation. Partner with Engineering to instrument product analytics, define meaningful dashboards, and establish feedback loops. Use A/B testing, phased rollouts, and other experimentation methods where appropriate to validate assumptions and improve outcomes.* Shape exceptional product experiences. Work closely with Design to create intuitive, polished experiences for complex B2B workflows. Bring strong product design judgment and be comfortable developing flows, wireframes, or prototypes when needed.* Identify opportunities for AI-native product development. Collaborate with Engineering to explore how AI, automation, and intelligent workflows can create real value for customers. Balance innovation with reliability, explainability, and trust.* Be the connective tissue across the business. Partner directly with our Head of Product, founders, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success. Bring customer and commercial context into product decisions, communicate tradeoffs, and keep teams aligned around the highest-impact work.## Must-Have* 5+ years of product management experience, including experience in a startup or high-growth technology environment.* Demonstrated end-to-end product ownership — you've independently owned meaningful product initiatives from problem discovery and strategy through execution, launch, and measurable impact.* Strong analytical thinking and product judgment — you can break down complex problems, define success metrics, evaluate tradeoffs, and make evidence-based decisions.* Proven ability to ship customer-facing software — you have a track record of working closely with engineers and designers to deliver high-quality products.* Demonstrable AI-native workflow — you can show how you've used AI tools to prototype, analyze, design, or accelerate your work.* Technical fluency — you understand APIs, integrations, data flows, and system architecture well enough to write precise requirements and collaborate credibly with Engineering.* Product design fluency — you have strong UX instincts and can contribute meaningfully to product flows, wireframes, and prototypes.* Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills — You can clearly articulate complex ideas, product decisions, and tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical audiences. You're equally comfortable collaborating with engineers, engaging directly with customers, and aligning senior leadership around a shared product vision.* Comfort operating with autonomy and ambiguity — you're resourceful, proactive, and capable of driving outcomes without extensive oversight.## Bonus Points* Engineering, Computer Science, or Product Design background — you've previously worked as an engineer, designer, or in another technical product-building capacity.* Founder or early-stage startup experience — you've built products or companies from the ground up and understand what it takes to operate with limited resources.* Accounts Receivable / Finance exposure — experience with invoicing, payments, cash application, credit workflows, or adjacent financial software.* Experience with AI-powered products — you've shipped LLM-powered features, automation, or intelligent workflows and understand the practical challenges of building reliable AI experiences.* Fintech or B2B marketplace background — experience navigating complex integrations, multi-stakeholder environments, or financial workflows.

Who Are We Looking to Add to Our Team?

jobs.description:
*This position is fully remote/home based. Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the following US states: FL, IL, MA, MD, NY, PA, TX, VA. This is a 2 Year FTC.

Role Summary

In this role you will oversee a subset of the growing PLOS journals portfolio: you will manage PLOS Biology and PLOS Medicine, with line-management of their professional Editors-in-Chief, and provide editorial oversight for a diverse set of journals led by academic volunteers across a range of disciplines in biology, human and environmental health. You will manage in line with PLOS strategy, helping to keep PLOS at the forefront of open science publishing and trusted content. You will leverage your strong relationships with the scientific community to drive engagement and develop the journals to meet the evolving needs of their global communities. You will work collaboratively with the journals’ Editorial Boards, and in-house colleagues, to create and deliver against journal strategies, using your international networks to grow PLOS’ profile and reputation.

The role is an integral part of the senior PLOS editorial leadership. As such, you will be expected to engage PLOS Leaders’ Framework—adaptive decision-making, empowering others, iterative learning, agility, resilience, systems thinking, continuous improvement, catalysing opportunity—at an advanced level. As part of that leadership, you will also own ad hoc projects across the entire PLOS journals portfolio. Priority projects currently relate to quality control, workflow optimization, cost efficiency, non-article research outputs (data and code), policy development and community engagement. You will embrace change, and lead your teams effectively through it.

Responsibilities

Journal portfolio management

  • Work closely with the Directors of Editorial, Publishing, MarComms and Global Development to develop an editorial strategy for a portfolio of PLOS journals that supports PLOS’s commitments to Open Science, DEI, community engagement, trusted content and customer service
  • Identify and develop opportunities to expand the portfolio in line with PLOS strategy
  • Develop and oversee attainment of multi-term performance metrics for individual journals
  • Partner with the Publishing Director to develop and manage annual budgets, ensuring responsible decision-making and efficient resource allocation to meet both budget and quality standards
  • Work closely with Operations colleagues and vendors to oversee optimization of editorial workflows, systems and reporting
  • Work closely with Marketing and Communications colleagues to ensure promotion of journal content and PLOS’ mission, and to drive journal submissions and uptake of Open Science practices
  • Ensure that Editorial makes effective and efficient use of cross-journal Centers of Excellence (e.g. Publication Ethics, Editorial Board Services)
  • Ensure that the portfolio shares cohesive and consistent editorial policies and quality standards, reacting dynamically to changing community needs while forefronting Open Science
  • Lead cross-journal initiatives, overseeing development of systems and workflows
  • Oversee Editorial participation in community initiatives, conferences and events, ensuring equality of opportunity and alignment with PLOS’ mission
  • Help to ensure best-practice document hygiene and information sharing by everyone in Editorial

People management

  • Lead a high-performing and cohesive team of Editorial staff (up to 4 direct reports), fostering a cross-portfolio and cross-cultural mindset
  • Ensure strategy is collaboratively translated into clear tactics for teams and individual staff, and monitor progress against goals regularly
  • Lead by example, modeling open and clear communication and ensuring all stakeholders understand their roles and responsibilities
  • Build strong relationships with Editorial Boards within a true partnership framework
  • Address underperformance swiftly, sensitively and supportively, in collaboration with Line Manager and People & Culture team
  • Act as a thought-partner to, and deputize for, the Editorial Director

Diversity, equity and inclusion

  • Oversee improvement of the diversity of PLOS staff, Editorial Boards, peer-reviewers and authors
  • Work collaboratively with stakeholders to eliminate bias in manuscript processing and editorial decision-making
  • Oversee editorial participation in internal and external DEI initiatives

Cross-sector

  • Maintain in-depth industry knowledge, awareness of market trends, innovations and evolving customer needs
  • Represent PLOS at industry events occasionally (approx 1-2 events per year)

Qualifications and Experience

  • PhD and post-doctoral experience (or equivalent) in a relevant subject area
  • Substantial editorial experience (5+ years) with progressively increased managerial responsibility in STM publishing required
  • Track record in managing a group of successful journals and teams distributed internationally
  • Passionate interest in science and scientists
  • Proven commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion in science and scholarly publication.
  • Strong business acumen
  • Wide network of contacts within global scientific communities
  • Demonstrated ability to think strategically, to innovate and to implement creative solutions
  • Experienced people manager with a track record of managing high-performing teams through change
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal

The base salary range we've established for these positions is $145,000 - $163,000. PLOS also offers a comprehenseive benefits package sumarized below.

US:

  • 401k with employer match
  • Employee sponsored health, dental and vision insurance (Dental and Vision 100% employer paid)
  • Paid Vacation, 11 public holidays and sick leave
  • Parental leave
  • Birthday and three winter holidays days off
  • Short term and long term disability insurance
  • 2 days paid time off for volunteering per year
  • Fully remote work environment with stipend on joining for home office

About PLOS

Building on a strong legacy of pioneering innovation, PLOS continues to be a catalyst in open science, reimagining models to meet open science principles, removing barriers and promoting inclusion in knowledge creation and sharing, and publishing research outputs that enable everyone to learn from, reuse and build upon scientific knowledge.

Our work is supported by a highly skilled global in-house team, partnerships with local scholarly organizations, and the valued contributions of a diverse, international community of scientific researchers.

At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors.

Kpler is expanding into high-value verticals where its extensive coverage of commodities and related supply chains gives customers a competitive edge. North American inland transportation is a key focus, supporting US and Canadian crude oil exports via pipelines, as well as the transportation of marginal barrels and last-mile movements via barges and rail.

As Product Manager for North America Inland Transportation Monitoring, you will own the product end to end, from strategy and roadmap through to the first release and go-to-market. Working closely with the Commodities Product and Business Unit Leads, you will identify market opportunities, translate customer needs into product requirements and build a product that delivers actionable insights across North American inland transportation.

You will work closely with Engineering, Data, Sales, Marketing and Market Analysts to develop a reliable, data-driven product, establish trusted methodologies and ensure seamless data delivery through web applications, APIs and other distribution channels.

This is an individual-contributor role for an experienced product professional with a background in commodities, transportation or an adjacent B2B data/SaaS environment. It offers the opportunity to build a new product category on a strong data foundation, taking a pragmatic, iterative approach rather than managing an already mature offering.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead product discovery to identify unmet customer needs and develop innovative propositions for internal and external customers.
  • Define the product strategy and roadmap for North America Inland Transportation Monitoring, prioritising development in collaboration with Product and Engineering teams.
  • Drive the first product release and go-to-market strategy, contributing to positioning, packaging and pricing input, and working with Sales and Marketing to support launch and early adoption.
  • Ensure seamless data delivery through web applications, APIs and other data distribution pipelines, working closely with Engineering and Data teams.
  • Establish trusted data standards and methodologies, using recognised external frameworks where relevant to ensure the product becomes a reliable reference source for customers.
  • Develop product positioning and competitive strategy, monitoring the North American inland transportation landscape and differentiating Kpler through its independent approach and real-time data infrastructure.
  • Collaborate across Product, Engineering, Data, Sales and Marketing to align teams around product development, customer value and go-to-market execution.
  • Implement product governance best practices and agile methodologies, maintaining effective prioritisation and delivery processes.
  • Analyse market feedback, delivery progress and product risks, keeping relevant stakeholders informed of roadmap trade-offs and potential challenges.

Skills & Experience

  • At least 7 years of product management or commercial experience in the commodities and transportation industries, or a closely related B2B data/SaaS business, with a track record of delivering products that customers adopt.
  • Strong understanding of the commodities and transportation data landscape, including the wider competitive environment.
  • Proven ability to translate customer needs into product direction and deliver solutions in close collaboration with Product and Engineering teams.
  • Experience with product discovery, roadmap prioritisation and data-product delivery.
  • Understanding of go-to-market planning, including product positioning, packaging and pricing input.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to work with databases and use complex data to develop impactful products.
  • Experience working across cross-functional teams to deliver data-driven products.
  • Fluency in English.
  • A rigorous, problem-solving approach, with the ability to operate independently and take ownership of outcomes.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to engage technical and commercial teams, including senior external stakeholders.
  • A pragmatic, action-oriented mindset, with the ability to operate in an ambiguous, early-stage environment and iterate towards product-market fit.

Nice to have

  • Direct experience in pipelines, rail or barges, rather than only adjacent transportation segments.
  • Experience launching a new product line rather than solely managing an established offering.
  • An established network across commodities trading houses, producers, operators or funds.
  • Understanding of the regulatory environment shaping North American pipeline, rail and barge transportation.

  • Comfort integrating with enterprise APIs such as ERP, BI platforms, SharePoint or Microsoft Graph, Teams, and REST/GraphQL services.
  • Solid SQL skills and working familiarity with a modern data platform (Databricks, Snowflake, or equivalent).

  • Strong problem-solving, communication, and documentation skills; comfortable demoing to business stakeholders and gathering requirements directly from subject-matter experts.
  • Familiarity with Git, CI/CD, and basic DevOps workflows.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility, or Power Platform (Power Apps, Power Automate).
  • Experience with Azure AI Foundry agents or Palantir AIP Logic / Workshop applications.

  • Prior experience delivering business applications in process industries, manufacturing, supply chain, or commercial analytics.

About the Role

As our Associate Advertising Campaign Manager, you'll help bring digital media campaigns to life for some of the world's leading CPG brands, agencies, retailers, and publishers. You'll own the day-to-day execution and performance of campaigns, from setup and launch through pacing, optimization, troubleshooting, and reporting, while partnering closely with Client Success and cross-functional teams to keep campaigns running smoothly. This is an entry-level advertising operations role that reports to our Director of Campaign Management.

This is a great opportunity for someone who is curious about how digital advertising works behind the scenes and enjoys working with data, problem-solving, and digging into the details. Prior ad tech experience is not required. We'll provide the training, mentorship, and support to help you build expertise in advertising technology and campaign management while taking on increasing ownership over time.

Responsibilities

  • Execute digital media campaigns across their full lifecycle, including setup, QA, launch, daily pacing, optimization, troubleshooting, reporting, and closeout
  • Set up campaigns accurately within Chicory's advertising technology and DSP platforms, following campaign requirements and instructions from the Client Success and Campaign Management teams
  • Monitor campaign delivery and performance, using data and tools such as Superset to identify trends, investigate anomalies, and surface opportunities to improve results
  • Implement and troubleshoot third-party tags and tracking solutions used for ad serving, impression measurement, user behavior, and sales attribution
  • Prepare recurring campaign reports and performance insights for internal and external partners, building toward greater autonomy over time

Qualifications

  • Enjoyment of working with data and technology, solving problems, and digging into the details
  • Strong organization and attention to detail, with a consistent sense of ownership and follow-through
  • Comfort learning new tools and systems, with curiosity and confidence when approaching unfamiliar technology
  • An analytical mindset and interest in understanding the “why” behind what’s happening in the data
  • Clear communication and effective collaboration with teammates across different functions
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment
  • Experience using spreadsheet tools to organize and analyze data, including functions such as pivot tables and VLOOKUPs, or motivation to strengthen these skills
  • Thoughtful problem-solving approach, with good judgment around when to work through an issue independently and when to ask for help or escalate

The base salary range for this position is $50,000 - $60,000 annually.

This is a remote role and we’re able to hire candidates who reside in the following states: Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Massachusetts, Michigan, Missouri, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, and Washington.

Our PhilosophyAt Chicory, we know that we are strongest when every person is valued, respected and treated with dignity. We actively put aside assumptions and judgment and work to make space for all points of view. We do serious work but don’t take ourselves too seriously. We consider our playful spirit a competitive advantage to building better relationships and finding the smartest solutions. We produce the best results by hiring smart people and giving them the space, safety and the resources to do their work. We are building a company people love working with and working at.

Our Commitment Statement to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, & Belonging

At Chicory, diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging are key ingredients in our recipe for success. Our diverse experiences, backgrounds, identities, and ways of thinking elevate the level at which we operate; this allows us to innovate in old-school industries by looking not at how things have been done, but how they should be done. We are building a workplace built on merit and equity where every one of us has a voice at the table.

Our Principles

  • Be Good People: The success of our company is totally dependent on having good, smart people.
  • Own It: We take pride in our work. When we see a problem, we step up. We hold ourselves, and each other, to the highest standard. We learn from mistakes, admit when we are wrong, and take full responsibility for delivering results, not just for our role, but for the mission.
  • Separate Your Ego From Your Position: We speak up with conviction, but we stay open to being wrong. Leadership isn’t about winning arguments or defending turf; it’s about serving the mission. We challenge ideas without taking it personally, and we invite feedback without getting defensive. Our goal is the best outcome, not to “be right.”
  • Find Reality: We pursue truth over comfort. We seek to understand before insisting on being understood. We dig beneath symptoms to uncover root causes, and we challenge assumptions, even our own. Clarity comes from curiosity, not certainty. We don’t settle for surface-level answers. We seek reality, even when it’s inconvenient.
  • Have a Beginner’s Mind: Just because something has been done a certain way doesn’t mean it’s the best way. We stay curious, challenge assumptions, and question the status quo. We stay innovative by tackling problems from a fresh perspective.
  • Bias for Action: Speed matters in business. We don’t wait for permission, perfect clarity, or endless alignment. We cut through noise, complexity, and politics to drive progress. When in doubt, we act, learn, and adapt because action beats indecision every time.
  • Customer Obsessed: Our customers are our North Star. We listen closely, dig deep to understand their needs, and deliver 5-star service at every touchpoint. We build products that actually work: simple, intuitive, and designed to solve real problems.
  • Above and Beyond: We don’t settle for “good enough,” we aim for exceptional. We go above and beyond what’s expected for our team, our customers, and ourselves. We stay curious and hungry. Every day is an opportunity to get better.

Role Description

Dropbox is hiring an Integrated Campaign Strategist to architect and orchestrate marketing campaigns for priority product launches and evergreen marketing motions. This role turns business priorities, audience insight, and product positioning into a clear campaign strategy that defines the audience, narrative, journey, channel roles, activation sequence, and measurement plan.

You will be the steward of how these campaigns show up in market across owned, earned, and paid channels. Working across Product Marketing, Brand and Creative, Comms, Web, Lifecycle, Paid Media, Content, Events, Marketing Operations, Analytics, and Sales, you will align teams around one integrated plan, connect individual activations into a coherent enterprise buyer experience, and guide the campaign from brief through launch, optimization, and learning.

This is a senior individual contributor role for a strategist who can lead through influence, make tradeoffs in ambiguity, and balance strong market storytelling with measurable business impact. You will help Dropbox bring important product stories to enterprise audiences with greater consistency, relevance, and effectiveness.

Responsibilities

  • Campaign strategy architecture: Translate mid-market and enterprise business goals, product positioning, audience insight, and market context into integrated campaign strategies for key launches and evergreen motions, including objectives, audience, narrative, journey, channel roles, phasing, and measurement.
  • Cross channel orchestration: Build and manage the integrated activation plan across owned, earned, and paid channels so that web, lifecycle, content, social, communications, events, partner, and media programs work as one connected campaign rather than separate channel plans.
  • In-market stewardship: Own the campaign through launch and sustainment, protecting the strategic throughline while ensuring creative, messaging, timing, and audience experience remain coherent across touchpoints and regions.
  • Cross-functional leadership: Establish the brief, operating rhythm, decision rights, milestones, dependencies, and readiness criteria that align Product Marketing, Brand and Creative, Communications, channel owners, Marketing Operations, Marketing Data Science, regional partners, and Sales.
  • Audience and journey design: Define target audiences and buying groups, map the role of each touchpoint across the customer journey, and ensure campaign experiences respond to buyer needs, market moments, and stages of consideration.
  • Performance and optimization: Partner with Marketing Data Science and channel owners to define full funnel success measures, synthesize owned, earned, and paid signals, identify what is driving or limiting performance, and recommend changes to audience, narrative, creative, sequencing, or channel mix.
  • Portfolio learning and scale: Capture campaign insights, codify reusable plays, distinguish enduring strategy from launch specific execution, and apply learning across the enterprise campaign portfolio to improve future launches and evergreen motions.

Requirements

  • 8+ years B2B marketing experience in integrated campaigns, enterprise marketing, product marketing activation, brand to demand, or a related discipline, ideally in SaaS or technology.
  • Direct experience building out campaign strategy and accountable to the outcome(pipeline generation, revenue generation).
  • Demonstrated ownership of complex integrated campaigns from strategy and brief through activation, optimization, and post campaign learning.
  • Strong campaign architecture skills, including audience definition, narrative development, buyer journey design, channel planning, phasing, and measurement.
  • Experience orchestrating owned, earned, and paid programs and understanding the distinct role each plays in building awareness, consideration, demand, and customer growth.
  • Ability to translate product positioning and enterprise customer insight into a cohesive market story and connected audience experience across multiple teams and touchpoints.
  • Strong cross functional leadership and program judgment, including the ability to establish decision rights, navigate competing priorities, resolve dependencies, and influence without direct authority.
  • Analytical fluency and experience using campaign, brand, engagement, and revenue signals to evaluate performance, communicate impact, and make optimization decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading enterprise product launch campaigns and building evergreen motions for a multi product B2B portfolio.
  • Experience partnering closely with Corporate Communications, analyst relations, customer advocacy, or social teams to connect earned programs with owned and paid activation.
  • Experience marketing to complex enterprise buying groups across industries, company sizes, regions, or stages of maturity.
  • Familiarity with marketing automation, CRM, media, intent, experimentation, and attribution platforms used to activate and measure integrated campaigns.
  • Experience using AI to accelerate research, briefing, content variation, synthesis, or analysis while retaining human ownership of strategy, judgment, and brand decisions.

Durable Skills

AI fluency means using these tools to amplify human judgment, not replace it. We believe people with these skills will thrive as work and technologycontinue to evolve:

  • Awareness:Understand yourself and others.
  • Judgment:Evaluate information and make decisions in complex situations.
  • Adaptability:Learn, adjust, and stay effective through change.
  • Connection:Communicate, collaborate, and build trust.

To learn more about why these skills matter and what the data shows about thriving through change, read this blog postfrom our Chief People Officer, Melanie Rosenwasser.
